subject: Math
subskill: Effect of Adding/Removing Data on Statistics
prompt:
Data set P consists of $11$ data values, each of which is the integer $8$. Data set Q consists of $12$ data values, eleven of which are the integer $8$, and one of which is the integer $150$.

Which of the following statements about the means and medians of data set P and data set Q is true?

choices.C: Both the means and the medians are different.
choices.D: Neither the means nor the medians are different.

explanation: Choice A is correct. The mean of a data set is the sum of the values divided by the number of values. The mean of data set P is $\frac{88}{11}$, or $8$. The mean of data set Q is $\frac{238}{12}$, or approximately $19.83$. Thus, the means are different. The median of a data set is the middle value when the values are ordered from least to greatest. The median of data set P is $8$, and the median of data set Q is the average of the two middle values, which are both $8$, so the median of data set Q is also $8$. Therefore, the medians are the same, so only the means are different.
